explanation: In Sri Lanka, growers cut the trees back so they sprout thin shoots, then peel the inner bark from these by hand; it curls into rolls called quills as it dries.

claims.text: Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of trees of the genus Cinnamomum.
Cinnamon is not made from the seed pods, roots or resin of a tree.
In Sri Lanka, cinnamon trees are cut back so they sprout shoots, and the inner bark is peeled from those shoots by hand.
Cinnamon bark curls into rolls called quills as it dries.

evidence.restatement: Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of trees of the genus Cinnamomum.
Cinnamon comes from bark, not from seed pods, roots or resin.
Ceylon cinnamon trees are coppiced so they send up shoots, and peelers strip the inner bark from the shoots by hand.

Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of Cinnamomum trees; cassia, the common cheap kind, is bark of related species.

claimResults.note: Rival reading tested: cassia bark is thicker and less often called inner bark, but it is still bark, and no option other than Inner bark is bark.

evidence.restatement: Cinnamon is not a resin, a root or a seed pod; vanilla and cardamom are the pod spices, ginger and turmeric the root spices.
In Sri Lanka the trees are coppiced into thin stems, the outer bark is scraped off, and the inner bark is peeled by hand.
The peeled inner bark dries into curled rolls called quills.
